On Justice Drive in Winton, two adjoining offices divide the job. Each keeps weekday hours through 5 p.m.

Hertford County tax offices
OfficeAddressPhone
Tax Assessor115 Justice Drive, Suite 4, Winton252-358-7810
Tax Collector115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, Winton252-358-7815

The assessor finds, identifies and appraises every taxable parcel and personal property account. The collector sends one bill that covers the county and the towns of Ahoskie, Harrellsville, Cofield, Como, Murfreesboro and Winton, plus two drainage districts, three fire districts and solid waste fees. Expect several lines on a single parcel's bill.

The due date is September 1. On January 6 a 2 percent charge begins, and 3/4 of 1 percent more is added monthly after that.

For mail, lateness is judged by the Postal Service postmark, never a meter stamp. You may make partial payments any time between receiving the bill and January 6. Escrow does not keep the bill from reaching you, since lenders are told electronically and decide which ones to pay, so phone your lender if it is meant to cover yours.

  • Pay online, at the Winton counter, or on the toll-free line at 1-888-520-8728.
  • Card payments online carry 2.5 percent, a processor fee the county never receives.
  • The counter takes cards too.
  • A returned check costs $25.00 or 10 percent of its amount, whichever is higher, up to $1,000 under G.S. 105-357(2).

Real estate values reset on January 1, 2027, the first reset since 2019. Under state rules, no more than eight years may pass between reappraisals.

Appraisers divide the county into market areas, also called neighborhoods, look at recent sales in each, and apply one schedule of values so comparable houses are measured alike. An outside appraisal firm with staff from North Carolina and Virginia is doing the work, and field measuring started in July 2025 to correct listing errors and record changes since the last round. A notice of assessed value comes soon after the effective date, with appeal steps printed on it. The tax office can pull the parcel's 2018 tax card if you want the old figures beside the new.

Values will not all move in step, because the aim is fairness between owners. Rates come from the commissioners and town boards, typically in June, and a bill equals value times rate, so request the rate sheet while planning a sale.

Your notice of assessed value explains how to appeal. Forms will also appear on the Assessor's page as the revaluation date nears.

Formal appeals go before the equalization and review board, which is usually the commissioners wearing a second hat. During a revaluation year it finishes by December 1. Your request to be heard has to be in before adjournment, and the assessor can tell you that date. See G.S. 105-322.

Only one of three state relief programs may be used by an owner: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, or the circuit breaker (G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1C and 105-277.1B). Apply through the county assessor on Form AV-9. State form income limit for 2026: $38,800.

Phone the Tax Assessor at 252-358-7810 to find out which program suits you and whether your parcel already has a filing. June 1 before the tax year is the last day to file, and the circuit breaker must be renewed each year. Selling can end a deferral, so bring it up before listing. The form is NCDOR Form AV-9.

Property tax stays with the land. G.S. 105-355 places a lien on real property as of the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs ride along. The owner named on the January 1 listing gets the bill, even if that person conveys later.

Steps for a seller:

  • Ask the collector for a payoff covering the current year and prior ones.
  • Let the closing attorney pay taxes from proceeds, language the Register of Deeds expects to see on deeds.
  • Hand any late-arriving bill to the buyer.

If a bill goes unpaid, the county can garnish wages, attach bank accounts or state income tax refunds, levy property and foreclose. Delinquent accounts can get a three-month payment plan. Auctions happen at the courthouse door, advertised in the local newspaper, and winners pay in full with cash or certified funds.

Before a house goes on the market, make three calls. The Tax Collector, 252-358-7815, can quote what clears the parcel. The assessor, 252-358-7810, can say whether a relief filing or deferral is attached. The tax office can send the rate sheet.

A sale near the 2027 revaluation will meet the new assessed value soon after January 1, 2027. Buyers' attorneys will see it, so learn the number and the appeal deadline early. Cash sales skip the lender's appraisal, but taxes still come out of proceeds at closing.

The Tax Collector also handles more than house bills. Motor vehicles are billed within 90 days of tag renewal, owners get one month to pay before interest starts, and after four months a block goes on the tag. The county cannot prorate or reduce a vehicle bill without the FS20 receipt from NCDMV, which must reach the office within one year of surrender. The license plate agency in Ahoskie is at 907 E. Memorial Drive.

The office lists county-owned property open for bids and foreclosed parcels with their auction dates. An outside attorney schedules foreclosure sales, and parcels that fail to sell at auction are sold by the county. You do not register ahead of time for an auction. You or a representative just appear at the courthouse door.

sections.h2: Homes and owners in Hertford County
sections.html:
The county has 8,285 households of about 2.20 people each. Owners hold 67.4 percent of the homes, and the middle-priced owned home is worth $119,200. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,285 a month, against $523 for those without. Parcels range from town lots in Ahoskie, Murfreesboro and Winton to cropland and timber, which is why the fire district and solid waste lines vary from one parcel to the next. Bring the collector's total to the closing table so nothing is left owing.

Housing costs are modest here, so a surprise tax bill at closing stings more than in a pricier market. Settle the payoff before the closing date, and confirm with the collector that the figure is current, since penalties and interest keep building each month after January 6.

faqs.q: How can I pay my Hertford County tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay online, in person at 115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, or by calling 1-888-520-8728. Online card payments add a 2.5 percent fee, and partial payments are accepted until January 6.

faqs.q: Which office sends the tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector bills for the county, six towns, fire and drainage districts, and solid waste fees. Call 252-358-7815 with questions.

faqs.q: When does the next revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The last one was in 2019, and owners receive notices of their new assessed values shortly after that date, with appeal instructions on the notice.

faqs.q: I sold my house but still got the bill. Why?
faqs.a: Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is the name on the bill, so one can still arrive after you sell. Send a copy to the new owner.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hertford County taxes over time?
faqs.a: Yes for delinquent accounts. The collector offers a three-month plan, and you can ask about it at 252-358-7815.
